title: Beyond Conventional Defenses: Proactive and Adversarial-Resilient Hardware Malware Detection using Deep Reinforcement Learning
problem: Machine learning-enabled hardware malware detection systems are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that circumvent their detection mechanisms, particularly on tabular processor performance counter data where traditional adversarial learning methods from image classification do not directly apply.
motivation: Adversarial attacks undermine the efficacy of ML-based hardware malware detection methods, creating critical security gaps in hardware protection.
method: The framework first generates adversarial attacks (intentional fake malware) to test whether standard ML detectors can be bypassed. It then trains a Deep Reinforcement Learning system (RL: a technique where systems learn to make decisions by receiving rewards for good choices and penalties for bad ones) using an Advantage Actor Critic algorithm to detect these attacks in real-time. The ML detectors themselves are strengthened through adversarial training—exposing them to intentional fake attacks so they learn to recognize similar real threats. Finally, the system automatically decides which defenses should activate at each moment using Upper Confidence Bounds (an algorithm for allocating limited resources intelligently), balancing protection with available computing power.
key_novelty: The system predicts adversarial attacks (fake malware attempts) targeting ML-based malware detectors in real-time using Deep Reinforcement Learning, automatically adjusting which specialized defenses activate based on available computing power.
contributions: Multi-phased adversarial learning and defense framework based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
Real-time adversarial attack pattern prediction using Advantage Actor Critic (A2C)
Adversarial training to enhance ML model robustness against combined malware and adversarial attacks
RL-based constraint controller using Upper Confidence Bounds for dynamic defense resource allocation
